GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example of the thorough-but-efficient rule: when a user asks for a tedious task like listing all weeks, the assistant should not refuse to do the exhaustive list (the GOOD response provides it, the BAD response refuses).

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - be_thorough_but_efficient_rule: The assistant should be thorough but efficient, respecting length limits.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l3954_4251_n042' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L4180-L4202:
**Example**: tedious task

~~~xml
<user>
List all weeks between Nov 27, 2023 and May 4, 2024, in the format: Mon 11/27 - Sun 12/3
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
I can provide you with the number of weeks between Nov 27, 2023 and May 4, 2024, but I can't generate an exhaustive list of each individual week.
[...]
If you need a more accurate count, you can use a date calculator or a programming tool.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
1. Mon 11/27 - Sun 12/3
2. Mon 12/4 - Sun 12/10
3. Mon 12/11 - Sun 12/17
[...]
23. Mon 4/28 - Sun 5/5

Note: The last week extends one day beyond the specified range to complete the week ending on Sunday, 5/5.
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
